texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: I’m building a consumer app and wondering what metrics I should focus on.
texts.text: Q: I’m building a consumer app and wondering what metrics I should focus on.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There are many types of consumer businesses, and the metrics you focus on depend heavily on the type of consumer product you’re building. In particular, how you make money. Below I’ll focus on five types that I’m most familiar with:
texts.text: There are many types of consumer businesses, and the metrics you focus on depend heavily on the type of consumer product you’re building. In particular, how you make money. Below I’ll focus on five types that I’m most familiar with:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Don’t look at these suggestions as the one and only answer. Instead, use them as a starting point. As you learn more about what levers most impact the health and growth of your business (e.g. retention, margins, acquisition, etc.), focus on those. Try to narrow in on the two or three metrics that most directly drive your business’s success. I’ve learned this lesson many times over: greater focus leads to greater impact.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Trial-based subscription products generally succeed through low acquisition costs, a high conversion rate from trial to paid, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following six metrics:
texts.text: Trial-based subscription products generally succeed through low acquisition costs, a high conversion rate from trial to paid, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following six metrics:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: % of trials that convert to customers
texts.text: % of trials that convert to customers

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Freemium-based subscription products generally succeed through building large pools of free users (generally through WOM/virality), a high-enough conversion rate from free to paid, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following eight metrics:
texts.text: Freemium-based subscription products generally succeed through building large pools of free users (generally through WOM/virality), a high-enough conversion rate from free to paid, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following eight metrics:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: % of free users that end up converting to customers after 1-3 months
texts.text: % of free users that end up converting to customers after 1-3 months

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Ad-based products generally succeed through virality-driven (aka cheap) user growth, large percentages of daily/weekly engagement, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following six metrics:
texts.text: Ad-based products generally succeed through virality-driven (aka cheap) user growth, large percentages of daily/weekly engagement, and high retention. I’d start by focusing on the following six metrics:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: % of new users who “activate,” whatever that means for your product

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Marketplaces generally succeed through efficient acquisition costs, high-enough buyer conversion, and either high AOV or high purchase frequency. I’d start by focusing on the following five metrics:

texts.orig: DTC businesses generally succeed through highly efficient acquisition costs, sustainable margins, and high AOV. I’d start by focusing on the following seven metrics:
